candidates.name: Practice Guide 11: inspection and official copies
verified_facts: Official copies of registers and title plans are dated or timed records and are admissible in evidence to the same extent as originals.
Pending applications may affect the temporal state represented by an official copy.
semantic_limits: Legal evidential status and document timing do not certify survey geometry or terrain elevation accuracy.

candidates.name: How to read a title plan
verified_facts: HM Land Registry explains that the title plan supports the register and uses red edging to indicate registered extent.
The guidance explicitly says red edging cannot be treated as the exact legal-boundary position and measurements scaled from the plan should not be relied on to locate a legal boundary.
semantic_limits: Title-plan scale and red edging cannot be converted into parcel height or centimetre-accurate geometry without independent survey evidence.
